H2232.d: to sow; figuratively, to disseminate, plant, fructify

H2233.d: seed; figuratively, fruit, plant, sowing-time, posterity

H2250.d: properly, bound (with stripes), i.e. a weal (or black-and-blue mark itself)

H2275.d: Chebron, a place in Palestine, also the name of two Israelites
fb: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.
Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Kohath's son, a Levite, and a clan of Levites came from him.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 3 men called Hebron. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in 1 Chronicles.

H2266.d: to join (literally or figuratively); specifically (by means of spells) to fascinate

H2280.d: to wrap firmly (especially a turban, compress, or saddle); figuratively, to stop, to rule

H2263.d: to clasp (the hands or in embrace)

H2224.d: properly, to irradiate (or shoot forth beams), i.e. to rise (as the sun); specifically, to appear (as a symptom of leprosy)

H2226.d: Zerach, the name of three Israelites, also of an Idumaean and an Ethiopian prince
fb: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Judah's son by Tamar, Perez's twin. His hand came out first and the midwife tied a scarlet thread on it, and then Perez was born ahead of him.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Not Judah's son. This Zerah is in the Genesis 36 family lists and in 1 Chronicles 1:37, one of the Idumaean names.
King living at the time of the Patriarchs
One of 6 men called Zarah. This one is a king from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A levite from the divided-kingdom years. 1 Chronicles names him twice.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
A man from the wilderness years, named twice across Numbers and 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

H2291.d: Chaggi, an Israelite; also (patronymically) a Chaggite, or descendant of the same
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Gad's second son, one of the seventy who went down into Egypt. The Haggite clan in the wilderness census came from him, and nothing else is recorded.

H2268.d: Cheber, the name of a Kenite and of three Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Not the Kenite. This Heber is in Genesis 46:17 among the family that went down to Egypt, and Numbers 26:45 makes him the head of a clan.
A Kenite, and his wife Jael killed Sisera in her tent when the Canaanite general came running. That fulfilled Deborah's word that a woman would get the credit.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 4 men called Heber. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

H2220.d: the arm (as stretched out), or (of animals) the foreleg; figuratively, force

H2203.d: asphalt (from its tendency to soften in the sun)

H2287.d: properly, to move in a circle, i.e. (specifically) to march in a sacred procession, to observe a festival; by implication, to be giddy

H2282.d: a festival, or a victim therefor

H2296.d: to gird on (as a belt, armor, etc.)

H2254.d: to wind tightly (as a rope), i.e. to bind; specifically, by a pledge; figuratively, to pervert, destroy; also to writhe in pain (especially of parturition)

H2213.d: a chaplet (as spread around the top), i.e. (specifically) a border moulding

H2239.d: the spread of the fingers, i.e. a span

H2219.d: to toss about; by implication, to diffuse, winnow

fb: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
They were Levites of Kohath's line, through his son Hebron. Under David they were put over Israelite land west of the Jordan and over treasuries tied to the temple.
Midianite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

Moses asked him to be Israel's guide out of Sinai, since he knew the wilderness. He was a Kenite related to Jethro, and Judges uses a word for him that has led some to think he was Jethro himself. His descendants settled near Jericho and later around Arad.

H2218.d: Zered, a brook East of the Dead Sea
fb: The Zered valley, the brook Israel crossed near the end of the wandering on the way around Edom and Moab.

H2227.d: a Zarchite or descendant of Zerach
fb: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
A descendant of Zerah. It shows up in the census lists and the rosters in Chronicles and never attaches to anyone well known.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Numbers names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
One of Zelophehad's five daughters. They asked Moses for their father's land, got it, and set a precedent for Israel.

H2277.d: a Chebrite (collectively) or descendants of Cheber
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Counted in Numbers 26, the clan of Heber, Asher's grandson through Beriah.
A point on the northern border of the land Moses described, southeast of Hamath. Nobody has found it.

H2256.d: a rope (as twisted), especially a measuring line; by implication, a district or inheritance (as measured); or a noose (as of cords); figuratively, a company (as if tied together); a throe (especially of parturition); also ruin

H2245.d: properly, to hide (as in the bosom), i.e. to cherish (with affection)

fb: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
She was one of David's wives and Adonijah's mother, and her son tried to take the throne while David was dying.

H2237.d: perhaps to diffuse, i.e. (specifically) to sneeze

fb: After Samaria fell in 722 BC, the Assyrians deported the northern kingdom's people to this river and its district. It is the Khabur, a big tributary of the Euphrates in what is now northeastern Syria.
Governor living at the time of Exile and Return
He came from David's line and led the first exiles back from Babylon to Jerusalem. As governor he laid the temple's foundation and, with Haggai and Zechariah pushing, saw it finished.

H2228.d: Zerachjah, the name of two Israelites
fb: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A priest in the high priestly line, one of the links between Ezra and Aaron.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ezra names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A Merarite Levite, in the line of Levi's descendants who served in the temple.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A Levite of Ladan's family, one of those David set over the temple treasuries.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
He was head of a big family that came back from exile, counted by household in both Ezra and Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

H2286.d: Chagaba or Chagabah, one of the Nethinim
fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Hagabah in Nehemiah's copy of the list. The family were temple servants, the Nethinim, home from exile with Zerubbabel.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
His descendants were temple servants, the Nethinim, who came back from Babylon with Zerubbabel. Nothing further is recorded about him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return

His family were priests who came back from Babylon and could not prove their descent from Aaron. They were kept out of the priesthood until a high priest could settle it with the Urim and Thummim, and the record never says that happened.

H2298.d: as card. one; as article single; as an ordinal, first; adverbially, at once

fb: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return

The exiles were back and building their own houses while God's temple stayed a ruin, and Haggai told them that was why they were struggling. His short book is dated to the month and day in 520 BC. He got the building going again, and Zerubbabel and the high priest Joshua finished it a few years later.
Governor living at the time of Exile and Return
He came from David's line and led the first exiles back from Babylon to Jerusalem. As governor he laid the temple's foundation and, with Haggai and Zechariah pushing, saw it finished.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of the seven eunuchs King Ahasuerus sent to bring Queen Vashti before his guests. She refused, and that set off everything that led to Esther.
Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
She was Haman's wife. She told him to build the gallows for Mordecai, and later, when things began to go wrong, told him he would fall before a Jew.

H2243.d: properly, a cherisher, i.e. the bosom

H2264.d: a clasping of the hands (in idleness)

H2223.d: properly, tightly girt, i.e. probably a racer, or some fleet animal (as being slender in the waist)

H2272.d: a streak (like a line), as on the tiger

fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Grandfather of Jaazaniah, the Rechabite leader Jeremiah tested with wine. Nothing else is recorded of Habazaniah himself.

H2235.d: something sown (only in the plural), i.e. a vegetable (as food)

fb: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy

He argued with God. Why does Judah's injustice go unpunished, he asks, and when the answer is Babylon, he asks how God can use a nation worse than Judah to do it. The book ends with him choosing to trust and rejoice with his questions still open, and his line that the righteous will live by faith is one Paul built on.
